title: Elevate Your Business: Essential Self-Care Practices for Leaders
author: Leadership With a Twist
summary: Coach Heather opens a five-part self-care series for leaders, arguing that self-care is not indulgence but a leadership fundamental because depleted, over-scheduled high performers can mask burnout for a long time simply by continuing to produce results. She reframes self-care as the foundation that enables clear thinking, sound decisions, and healthy relationships, insisting that no one else can answer what a leader's body and mind actually need. The piece closes with a low-stakes five-minute reflective exercise, prompting leaders to notice, without yet fixing, what they need more of.
points: Argues capable people can compensate for burnout for a long time, which makes the depletion more dangerous, not less.
Reframes self-care as a leadership responsibility rather than a reward earned after serving everyone else.
Provides self-diagnostic questions about what helps a leader function, what drains them, and where they override their own signals.
Ends with a low-stakes five-minute practice rather than a demanding new regimen.
quotes: When you are highly capable, you can compensate for depleted energy for a long time. You can keep producing and showing up, and because everything is still getting done, it can be easy to assume everything is fine.

Self-care is not only about avoiding burnout. It is about creating the conditions that help you think clearly, make good decisions, regulate your emotions, maintain healthy relationships, recover from challenges, and enjoy the life you are working so hard to build.
Other people can support us, but we are the ones living inside our own bodies and experiencing our energy, emotions, thoughts, and limits every day.
Sometimes taking better care of yourself begins with deciding that your own needs are important enough to pay attention to.

I have worked with so many capable, committed people who can accomplish an extraordinary amount even when they are tired, stressed, over-scheduled, or running on fumes. I know that pattern personally, too.
